contacts.institution: U.S. Congressman Leo Ryan's congressional delegation visiting Jonestown (U.S. Congress)
contacts.when: November 18, 1978, during the delegation's visit to Jonestown
contacts.what_was_asked: To be taken out of Jonestown with the congressman's party (defect).
contacts.what_institution_did: The congressman accepted the family's request and had them board the truck to the airstrip to be flown out with his party.
contacts.quote: So we all went down to tell Ryan we were leaving. And then when we went down and told him that, then it started growing. And so first was the park's family, then it was my family, and then there were some others that started telling them they wanted to leave too. So the next thing Ryan knew is he had a group on his hands that wanted to leave. Everything wasn't rosy and paradise. And that was the first news he got of it that away because until then it had been playing the role. persons.outcome_quote: That's when I get shot get the back of my leg blown off and that's when she gets shot in her leg also with 22 which rattles around who goes down of bone and comes back out of ankle.
persons.decisive_work_quote: I think it's important to highlight that without the push of Congressman Ryan and journalists like Tim Reiterman investigating Jonestown, the Boge family, as well as the other defector families may not have lived that day.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: The first institutional contact (the congressman's delegation, November 18, 1978) acted the same day, after roughly 13 years in the temple.
persons.notes: Outcome reasoning: the congressman's acceptance of the family's request got Tom out of Jonestown on the day of the mass murder (the host says the families 'may not have lived that day' without it), but he was then shot under the delegation's escort, and a cursory search missed a gunman, so 'partly_protected' rather than 'protected'. The leader's death the same day also ended the harm; the outcome is debatable between partly_protected and not_protected. Not coded as contacts because the harm was not shown to be raised: at age 9 a maintenance worker 'called it in' after he ran away; 'They picked me up. I spent the night in some church in a Modesto' and he was sent to his aunt's; who 'they' were and what he told them is unclear (s4-e1 @ 17:35). His aunt and uncle (family) were told everything at age 14 but called his mother, who came with temple enforcers (s4-e3 @ 34:16-35:18). Evidence: Tom's 2013 essay is read on air (s4-e3 @ 27:58 onward); Jim corroborates; narration draws on books by Julia Scheeres and Tim Reiterman and, per the host, FBI documentation (s4-e3 @ 3:22). Later PTSD, drug use and homelessness (s4-e6 @ 13:27).

Tom says the district attorney and some deputies were temple members (s4-ep3 @ 18:50). He was denounced in front of the community after his wife reported him to the leader (s4-e5 @ 1:01).

persons.notes: The season does not say what finally happened to him (whether he left with the defectors or died on November 18), so 'deceased' is false only by default. 'other' reasons: his father kept him in the temple; he and Tom tried to reach a military post to contact the U.S. consulate but were caught first. The shackles were taken off at the Jonestown nurses' station on the order of the leader's family (temple-run, not an outside institution). Evidence: Tom's essay read on air and Tom's interview.

persons.name: Bob Houston
persons.harm: A long-time temple member who defected and was found crushed between rail cars in a San Francisco train yard in 1976; Tom and Jim believe he was killed as a warning to others who left.
persons.perpetrator_role: the People's Temple leader (alleged by the interviewees)

contacts.when: After his death in 1976, before November 1978
contacts.what_was_asked: His father asked the congressman, a long-time friend, to help look into the suspicious death and to help reconnect him with his granddaughters, still being raised in the church.
contacts.what_institution_did: The congressman agreed to help and, also prompted by a newspaper article and the Concerned Relatives group, went to Jonestown with journalists and relatives.
contacts.quote: After Bob died, his father Sammy approached his friend the Congressman about helping him look into the suspicious death of his son and helping reconnect with his granddaughters, whom were still being raised by their mother in the church. Congressman Leo generously agreed to do his best to help his friend find answers.
contacts.what_happened_next: The congressman visited Jonestown and was killed at the airstrip; the season reports no finding about the death.
contacts.notes: Basis: host narration drawn from books (Raven; A Thousand Lives). The father also worked with a journalist (author of Raven) at the Associated Press, which is how that journalist learned of the alleged abuse and possible murders of defectors (s4-e5 @ 6:14); journalists are not an institution under the codebook.

persons.outcome_quote: Bob Houston, he was in San Francisco, there somewhere, but he was killed in the train yards. He said it was a suicide, but we know it wasn't.
persons.notes: He died before any contact, so not_protected. 'He said it was a suicide' — who 'he' is (an official, or someone else) is not said; it may mean his death was officially called a suicide, but that is not clear enough to code as a contact.

persons.name: Patricia (Patti) Parks
persons.harm: A Jonestown member whose family was the first to ask the congressman to take them out; shot dead on the plane in the airstrip attack.
persons.perpetrator_role: airstrip gunmen sent from the temple

contacts.institution: U.S. Congressman Leo Ryan's congressional delegation (U.S. Congress)
contacts.what_was_asked: To leave Jonestown with the congressman's party.
contacts.what_institution_did: Accepted the defectors and put them on the truck to the airstrip to be flown out.
contacts.quote: So we all went down to tell Ryan we were leaving. And then when we went down and told him that, then it started growing. And so first was the park's family, then it was my family, and then there were some others that started telling them they wanted to leave too. So the next thing Ryan knew is he had a group on his hands that wanted to leave. Everything wasn't rosy and paradise. And that was the first news he got of it that away because until then it had been playing the role. So he said, okay, you know, as well, you guys go get on the truck and, you know, we're gonna start heading out to the airport.
contacts.what_happened_next: She was shot dead on the plane when temple gunmen attacked at the airstrip.
contacts.notes: Tom: 'we heard that the the parks family had gone to Ryan and told them they wanted to leave.' (s4-e5 @ 12:29).

persons.outcome_quote: And at that point, Patti Parks, who was sitting right in front of me in the airplane, I'm sitting right across from the door. She gets the back of her head shot off.
persons.notes: Died from the harm, so not_protected under the codebook even though the institution accepted her request. Her death is confirmed in host narration (s4-e6 @ 2:03).

coder_notes: Season 4 ('Escaping Jonestown') tells the Bogue family's People's Temple story through interviews with Tom and Jim and narration drawn from books (Raven by Tim Reiterman; A Thousand Lives by Julia Scheeres), Tom's 2013 essay, and, per the host, FBI documentation. All three chunk files were read to their last lines. s4-e8 is a COVID-19 mental-health interview with no harm stories. Main coding judgment: the family's one effective institutional contact was the congressman's delegation, which accepted their request to leave on November 18, 1978; they were attacked at the airstrip under its escort (Tom and Tina shot), so survivors are coded partly_protected and the decisive worker is unclear (the visit came from a defector's father, a newspaper article, the Concerned Relatives group and journalists). A reader could argue for not_protected, since the leader's death that day also ended the harm. Tom (and Jim) say the district attorney and some sheriff's deputies were temple members and that officials 'turned a blind eye' to reports of abuse; the season names no specific report to an outside institution before 1978. Several institution encounters were not coded as contacts because the harm was not raised (Tom's age-9 runaway pickup; a sheriff's deputy serving eviction papers on Jim; a county stop of the stolen-food truck). Perpetrator names, including the airstrip gunman's, are replaced with [perpetrator] in quotations. The task note's framing ('institutions usually do their jobs well') was not used as evidence; coding follows the transcripts.
